newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA LOSE UNBEATEN RECORD IN 2-1 DEFEAT AT BILBAO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA LOSE UNBEATEN RECORD IN 2-1 DEFEAT AT BILBAO.

text.p: Spanish league leaders Barcelona lost their unbeaten record after going down 2-1 at Athletic Bilbao in a rain-soaked clash on Saturday.
Second-placed Real Madrid will go top by one point if they beat Valencia on Sunday, while Athletic move up from sixth to fourth, seven points behind Barcelona.
Athletic opened strongly, but Barcelona took the lead through defender Abelardo Fernandez, who rose unmarked to head home a Josep Guardiola corner after 25 minutes.

Athletic struck back after 62 minutes when former Barcelona midfielder Jose Mari Garcia knocked in a loose ball, and the Basques took the lead 15 minutes from the end when captain Julen Guerrero thundered home a rebound after a free kick bounced off the Barcelona wall.
After a quiet game Brazilian striker Ronaldo nearly saved a point for Bobby Robson's side when he headed a cross from Luis Figo against the bar with just a minute from time.
The match was marked by several disputed penalty decisions which caused tension between Athletic coach Luis Fernandez and the Barcelona bench.
